idiom_name: JAXP-style abstract class with newInstance() + subclass factories
implementation_notes: The JDK provides the pattern in JAXP: DocumentBuilderFactory and SAXParserFactory are abstract classes whose newInstance() performs provider lookup and whose newDocumentBuilder()/newSAXParser() operations create parser products. Model your own families on that shape - an abstract class or interface with one creation method per product kind, one implementation per family - and bind the chosen implementation through the composition root (DI container or registry), so clients depend only on the abstract type. javax.inject.Provider/Supplier<T> are lighter alternatives for single-product seams but do not carry family consistency; sealed interfaces plus pattern matching help when the family set is closed and compiler-checked. ServiceLoader is useful for open plugin families, but providers are discovered and instantiated lazily and cached per loader, so do not assume a process-wide singleton; choose and document the factory lifetime explicitly.
pitfalls: newInstance() can honor a system property and other external lookup inputs, so an untrusted deployment can select a different parser provider; validate the provider and harden parser features against XXE before parsing untrusted XML.
Static singletons (getInstance()) hide the family dependency and make tests order-dependent; inject the abstract factory instead.
Adding a product kind changes the abstract class and every subclass across modules, so JDK-style factories stay deliberately narrow.

JAXP newInstance() reports provider-loading failures with FactoryConfigurationError (an Error), not InitializationException; catch or surface the documented failure deliberately instead of naming the wrong exception.

ServiceLoader discovers providers lazily and reload() clears its cache; assuming the first provider is instantiated once for the whole process creates accidental shared state, so select and scope providers explicitly.
